2. As per the quarterly report received from field offices the total amount of
monthly claims towards Employer’s Contribution in respect of disabled employees
appointed on or after 01.04.2008 is Rs.90,65,195/- as on 30.06.2013. The list of the
offices to which this amount pertains is enclosed herewith for verification. The concerned
field offices may verify the amount shown against their office.

sought guidelines from Head Office on reimbursement of employer’s share of contribution
deposited by the employers in respect of persons with disabilities employed on or after
01.04.2008. The above offices have requested for providing fund from Central Account for
reimbursement of employer’s share to the employers. For the purpose of reimbursement of
individual claims received from the employers under the Incentive Scheme, the following
exercise is to be carried out by the field offices at their level before the reimbursement is
made to the employer:

(1) Ensure that the employers have engaged the employees with disabilities
covered under the Incentive Scheme for disabled employees circulated vide
Head Office circular letter No. Coord.Misc./2007/3907 dated 08.05.2008.
The disabled employees should be appointed by the employer on or after
01.04.2008 with monthly wages upto Rs.25,000/- per month.

(ii) The Employers Contribution to the Employees’ Provident Fund is to be
reimbursed for the first three years only.

(iii) The accuracy of the claim of the employer has to be certified by the
concerned RPFC In-charge of the region. Besides the regions should keep
full proof record containing the details of the employers/employees, their
date of appointment, wage, subsidies claimed, general compliance position
of the establishment etc.

(iv) After verification of the claims of the employers the field offices may
reimburse the amount of employer’s share. There will not be any physical
transfer of money from Hars. to regions towards reimbursement of
employer’s share of contribution. The amount so reimbursed is to be
booked in the annual accounts for adjustments with the Central Account of
Head Office. In this regard instructions will be issued separately.

employed under the Incentive Scheme under eighteen numbers of Regional Offices and
the amount to be reimbursed is reported to Head Office. Instructions have been issued
from time to time to Regional/Sub-Regional Offices to take steps for awareness of the
benefits of disability scheme and to improve the coverage of disabled persons by
contacting Vocational Centers/NGO under their jurisdiction to educate them on the
benefits under the Incentive Scheme and also to organize regular seminar and workshops
with employers’ organization to enhance employment of disabled persons. The field
offices are again advised to take appropriate action in this regard for awareness of the
Disability Scheme and to improve the coverage of disabled persons.

Office on regular basis. The said report should reach to Head Office by 10" of the

Subject: - Attachment of bank accounts for enforcing appearance.

Sir,

Instances have been noticed in which the officers conducting inquiries u/s
7A have issued orders to attach/freeze bank accounts of the establishments/ personal
accounts of the employers for alleged non-appearance in such inquiries. Such

practices have attracted a lot of adverse observations from Constitutional Courts and

other quarters.

In so far as the power to impose fines for non-appearance, by invocation of
section 32 CPC is concerned, it may be noted that the power of a Civil Court, and

consequently an officer exercising jurisdiction under section 7A, in imposing a

pecuniary fine for willful absence of a party summoned, is restricted to the amount

of Rupees Five thousand only by virtue of section 32, 1bid.

The power to attach and sell property for non-appearance is also subject to

limitations prescribed in rule 10 of Order XVI of the CPC which circumscribes the

power so available to the limit of fine imposable under rule 12. Alternatively stated,
when the power to attach and sell property of the employer is sought to be exercised
for non-appearance, the value of property so attached has to be within the quantum

of fine that could be levied under the relevant provision.

It has been observed, in a number of cases, that the officers issue attachment
orders without specifying any amount to the extent of which the attachment is
intended to be made. It is important to note that the power to make attachments of
unlimited value or to freeze operation of bank accounts is not relatable to any

provision of the Act or Code of Civil Procedure. Such actions are evidently illegal

and amount to blatant misuse of authority besides causing unwarranted harassment

to the employers concerned.

All adjudicating officers are, therefore, advised to take note of the legal

provisions. Any violation will invite strict disciplinary action.

Subject: Instructions regarding defending matters relating to constitutional/legal

validity of statutory provisions/executive directions.
Madam/Sir,

It is seen that challenges to constitutional or legal validity of statutory provisions of
the Act/Schemes, Gazette Notifications or policy decisions of EPFO in various constitutional
courts are dealt with and defended by concerned Regional Offices. Many such cases, it has

been noticed, are defended without seeking instructions from Head Office.

EPFO and Union of India are necessary parties in cases where statutory provisions or
notifications are challenged for their constitutional or legal validity. Similarly, cases
involving challenge to any policy decision or executive direction of EPFO would have the
Headquarters as a necessary party. The defense of such cases by the respective RPFCs, even
when Headquarters/Uol are not arrayed as parties, is improper and legally unsustainable.
The current practice adopted by Regional Offices also leads to inadequate defense of the

challenge and sometimes leads to irremediable situations.

It is therefore directed that in cases where policy decisions of EPFO, statutory
provisions or any Gazette Notification under the Act or any of the Scheme are challenged,
the concerned Regional Office should refer the matter to Legal Division, Head Office for

instructions. No submission on merits of the matter should be made in such cases without

approval of the headquarters.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

Yours faithfully

Term Limit:  The Presiding Officer and committee members hold office for a maximum period of three years from their date of nomination.

OVERVIEW
Eﬃcient governance supported by sound actuarial practices is essential to the long-term sustainability of social security systems.
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), one of the largest social security institutions in the world, manages retirement
savings, pension, and insurance schemes for millions across India. Given its scale and complexity, actuarial work at EPFO plays
a strategic role beyond statutory valuations. It informs sustainability analysis, nancing strategies, investment governance, and
policy reform decisions.
This programme, developed by the International Training Centre of the ILO (ITCILO) in collaboration with the ILO DWT/CO-New Delhi,
is situated within the broader ILO project on Promoting and Building Social Protection in South Asia, which seeks to strengthen
sustainable, inclusive, and gender-transformative social protection systems, with a focus on extending social insurance, improving
coverage, benet adequacy, nancial sustainability, and gender equality. The project also emphasises institutional capacity-building,
tripartite social dialogue, and regional knowledge-sharing as foundations for resilient and equitable social protection reform.
Building on the ILO and International Social Security Association (ISSA) Guidelines on Actuarial Work in Social Security and Good
Governance, as well as ITCILO’s longstanding experience in actuarial practice and pension reform capacity development worldwide,
the programme aims to strengthen actuarial governance and integrate high-quality actuarial analysis into EPFO’s governance
and decision-making processes. It promotes the use of actuarial work as a strategic governance tool to strengthen accountability,
transparency, nancial sustainability, and evidence-based decision-making in social security institutions, in line with ISSA Good
Governance principles.
The course focuses on high-level strategic issues related to pension system governance, nancing, and reform. Key topics include
governance frameworks, nancing models, sustainability challenges, reform options, and the strategic use of actuarial evidence.
The course emphasizes the role of senior leadership in ensuring sound nancial governance, eective oversight of social security
funds, accountability in decision-making, and long-term institutional sustainability.

Subject: Uniform validation, updating and closure of litigation records in LIMBS - standing
instructions

1. A review of LIMBS records shows recurring gaps in the party details, identification of the offices
concerned, description of the dispute, present stage, counsel details, next action and final outcome.
Entries such as 'PF matter’, 'pension dispute’, ‘appeal filed’, 'non-payment of dues’, 'prosecution case’ or
‘contempt pending’ are not adequate.

2. LIMBS is EPFO's official litigation register. Its accuracy is part of case management, compliance,
recovery, appeal control and accountability.
I. FIELDS TO BE VALIDATED

3. The exercise shall cover the Petitioner, Respondent, Brief History, Status Head, Date Type, Date,
Updated By and Updated On fields. Any other incorrect field, including Court, case number or filing
date, shall also be corrected or referred through the LIMBS nodal mechanism.

Il, PETITIONER AND RESPONDENT

4. The Petitioner and Respondent fields shall reproduce the judicial cause title. They shall not be altered
merely to show the office handling the case.

5. Where the cause title uses only 'EPFO', 'Central Board of Trustees' or another general description,
the responsible offices shall be identified in the Brief History.

Il. TWO DISTINCT OFFICES

6. Every record shall distinguish the Litigation-Handling Office from the Subject-Matter Office
wherever they are different.

(a) Litigation-Handling Office: the RO/ZO/Head Office Division Peapprnihle for counsel, appearance,
filing, hearing, communication of orders and LIMBS updating.

Page |

(b) Subject-Matter Office: the RO/ZO/Head Office Division whose member account, establishment,
assessment, pension decision, service matter, recovery, IBC claim, administrative action or records
gave rise to the case.

7. The Subject-Matter Office shall verify the facts, supply records and instructions, take substantive or
compliance action and examine further remedy. The Litigation-Handling Office shall conduct and
monitor the proceeding. One office shall not shift its duty to the other.

8. The Brief History shall state:
Litigation-Handling Office: RO/ZO/HO Division . Subject-Matter Office: RO/ZO/HO
Division :
9. Where one office performs both roles, the entry may state: Litigation-Handling and Subject-Matter
Office:
IV. SPECIAL ALLOCATION CASES

10. In a consumer case filed at the complainant's place of residence, the office responsible for that
Consumer Commission shall be the Litigation-Handling Office. The office which dealt with the PF
account, PPO, claim or decision shall be the Subject-Matter Office.

Illustration: Litigation-Handling Office: RO Kannur. Subject-Matter Office: RO Kanpur.
11. In NCLAT matters, the ACC/office assigned to the Delhi or Chennai Bench shall be the Litigation-
Handling Office. The RO/ZO which dealt with the corporate debtor, assessment or EPFO claim shall

be the Subject-Matter Office. Delay in filing, refiling, removal of defects, records, approval or
instructions shall be attributed to the office responsible for that stage.

V. BRIEF HISTORY - MINIMUM CONTENT

12. The Brief History shall enable a reviewing officer to understand the case without first calling for
the physical file. It shall state:

(i) the Litigation-Handling Office and Subject-Matter Office;
(ii) the exact dispute, not merely its broad category;

(iii) EPFO's role in the proceeding;

(iv) the material order, action, omission or default;

(v) the amount and period, where relevant;

(vi) the actual procedural stage;

(vii) the advocate presently engaged; and

(viii) the next action and the office responsible for it.

13. 'Pension matter’ shall specify the pension issue. 'PF matter’ shall specify settlement, transfer, KYC,
death claim, EDLI, non-remittance, exemption, recovery or other issue. 'Service matter’, 'IBC matter’
and 'prosecution matter’ shall likewise state the precise issue.

14. Where the Court field is generic, the exact Court or Bench shall be stated. This is mandatory for
subordinate-court matters shown only under a generic District and Sessions Court entry.
VI. CASES INSTITUTED BY EPFO

15. Where EPFO is petitioner, appellant, complainant or applicant, the Brief History shall also state the
office on whose behalf the case was filed, the order or default challenged, relief sought, amount and

Page 2

period, date of receipt or cause of action, filing date, limitation, approval to file where required, interim
relief and its status.

16. An entry stating only 'EPFO filed appeal’, 'EPFO is petitioner’, ‘prosecution filed’ or 'SLP filed! is
incomplete.

VII. MONEY, ORDERS AND STAGE

17. Where money is involved, the nature, period, total amount, amount admitted, paid, deposited or
recovered, and balance in dispute shall be stated. Composite demands shall show the Section 7A,
Section 7Q, Section 14B, EDLI and charge components, where available.

18. Where an order or action is challenged, the Brief History shall state its date, issuing authority,
substance, effect and the relief sought.

19. 'ONGOING' is not a procedural stage. The actual stage shall be stated, such as notice, service,
counter, evidence, arguments, judgment reserved, compliance, execution, cognizance, summons,
appearance, bail or warrant.

20. The next action shall be specific. It shall identify the action, the responsible office or officer, and a
target date where the action lies within EPFO's control.

VIL. ADVOCATE
21. As LIMBS has no separate counsel field, the Brief History shall state:

Advocate presently engaged: Shri/Smt , Panel Counsel/Standing Counsel/AOR, engaged
on

22. If counsel has not been engaged, the entry shall state the office responsible and the date by which
engagement is due. Substitution of counsel and papers or instructions pending with counsel shall also
be recorded.

IX. CONTEMPT, CONNECTED CASES AND CLUSTERS

23. Every contempt entry shall identify the original case, underlying subject, operative direction,
alleged default, compliance, appeal or review, stay position, present stage and next action. Filing an
appeal does not suspend compliance unless a stay or modification has been granted.

24. Each case shall retain a separate LIMBS record. Lead and connected cases may be cross-referenced.
Prosecutions against the same establishment may be shown as a monitoring cluster without merging
the individual cases.

25. Standard wording may be used only after verifying the individual party, case number, office, order,
amount, period and facts. Copying another case's history without verification is a data-quality defect.

X. DISPOSAL AND ARCHIVING
26. A case shall not be archived merely because the judicial portal shows it as disposed.

27. Before archiving, the Brief History shall record the date and type of disposal, the operative result,
whether the outcome is favourable, adverse or mixed, the financial effect, compliance, further remedy,
limitation and any remanded or consequential proceeding.

28. A disposed matter shall not be treated as finally closed while compliance, recovery, appeal, review,
remand or other consequential action remains.

29. Status Head and Date Type shall reflect the actual position. A disposed case shall not remain shown
as ongoing. Elapsed next dates, placeholder dates and incorrect dates shall be verified.

30. Updated By shall identify the officer, designation and office:

31. Where Updated By is drawn from the user profile, the profile shall show the officer's current
designation and RO/ZO/Head Office Division. A transferred officer shall not continue to use a profile
carrying the previous office.

32. Updated By is an audit trail. It does not replace identification of the Litigation-Handling and
Subject-Matter Offices in the Brief History.

XII. DRAFTING, PRIVACY AND SYSTEM LIMITS

33. The Brief History shall be factual, concise and neutral. It shall not reproduce pleadings, arguments
or opinions. Unnecessary personal data, Aadhaar and bank details shall not be entered. Member
identifiers may be masked unless full details are operationally necessary.

34. Where a dedicated editable field exists, it shall be used. Where it does not, the information shall be
entered in Brief History. An uneditable error shall be recorded in Brief History and referred through
the nodal mechanism.

XIU. VALIDATION AND CERTIFICATION

35. All active cases shall be reviewed. Priority shall be given to contempt, cases older than five and ten
years, high-value and policy matters, cases instituted by EPFO, adverse disposals, elapsed dates,
unclear office responsibility and cases shown as disposed but not properly closed.

36. The Officer-in-Charge of the RO shall certify the accuracy and usability of the records. The ZO
shall verify contempt, cases older than ten years, high-value and policy matters, adverse disposals,

cases instituted by EPFO, unresolved responsibility and a reasonable sample of the rest. Head Office
Divisions shall validate matters handled or owned by them.

37. This is a continuing duty. Brief History shall be updated after every material order, change of stage,
compliance, appeal, stay, change of counsel or disposal.

38. Where records are incomplete or responsibility is disputed, the entry shall state the verified position,
the unresolved point, the office responsible and the next action. Silence is not an option.

B. Operational clarifications
Which cases are to be updated?
All active cases and all cases shown as pending or ongoing. Disposed cases wrongly shown as
pending shall be corrected before archiving.

Page 13

What if LIMBS has no dedicated field?
Enter the information in Brief History. Refer system corrections through the LIMBS nodal
mechanism.

Are all template fields mandatory?
Only fields relevant to the case.

How long should Brief History be?
Concise but complete. It is not a synopsis of pleadings.

What if the two offices are different?
State both. The handling office manages the case; the subject office supplies facts and takes
substantive action.

What if responsibility is unclear?
Record: 'Responsibility under verification; action with by . The ZO or
concerned Head Office Division shall resolve it.

What if old records are unavailable?
Do not guess. Record: 'Record reconstruction/verification in progress; action with by
'
Should the advocate be named?
Yes. LIMBS has no separate counsel field.
Does an appeal suspend compliance?
No. State whether the order has been stayed or modified.
What is present stage?
The actual procedural stage, not ‘ongoing’.
What is next action?
A specific action, responsible office or officer, and target date where within EPFO's control.
How are connected cases handled?
Keep separate records and cross-reference the lead or connected matter.
What if the Court record conflicts with LIMBS?
Verify the latest authentic judicial record and record the date of verification.
Can a disposed case be archived at once?
No. First record the disposal, effect, compliance, further remedy and limitation.
Is this a one-time exercise?
No. The standard applies to every new case and every material development.
